Melanoma is the deadliest form of skin cancer, characterized by high metastatic potential and intrinsic heterogeneity. In addition to genetic mutations such as BRAF^V600E^ and NRAS, lipid metabolic reprogramming has emerged as a critical factor in tumor progression and therapy resistance. Lipid metabolism supports melanoma cell survival, phenotypic switching, immune evasion, and resistance to targeted therapies and immunotherapy, while also modulating susceptibility to ferroptosis.
